name: 6.2 Small-Block V8 NA
notes: Variant: Chevrolet Corvette Stingray (C8, LT2 6.2 L = 6,162 cc) with the Z51 Performance Package (performance exhaust: 495 hp / 369 kW at 6,450 rpm, 470 lb-ft / 637 Nm at 5,150 rpm; electronic limited-slip differential; Z51-specific axle ratio) and the M1L 8-speed dual-clutch transaxle (designed with TREMEC), on the standard Z51 rear (driven) tyre 305/30ZR20 (Michelin Pilot Sport 4S; front 245/35ZR19). Gear ratios 2.905/1.759/1.220/0.878/0.653/0.508/0.397/0.329 (reverse 2.632) and final drive 5.17 are from GM Specialty Vehicles' MY26 C8 Corvette Stingray specifications (Australian market, where Z51 is standard); the US Z51 car uses the same 5.17 (EPA Test Car List axle ratio 5.17). GM lists a single final drive, so overall ratio = gear x 5.17 for every gear; no other gear stage is applied. A 3.55 'ring and pinion' figure circulating for the C8 cannot be the overall reduction (8th x 3.55 would give N/V 14.9 against the EPA's 22.0). Checks: EPA MY2022-2025 Corvette (495 hp, 8 gears, RWD, axle 5.17) N/V 22.0, model 21.67 (-1.5 %; the MY2024 list also has a 5.17 row at N/V 21.8); the non-Z51 car (mechanical LSD, axle 4.89, EPA N/V 20.6, model with 4.89: 20.49) and the E-Ray (5.17, N/V 21.3 on 345/25ZR21, model 21.21) are not modelled but corroborate the ratios; GM's owner-manual paddle-downshift inhibit speeds for Z51 vs non-Z51 (4th 102 vs 108 mph, 5th 144 vs 152 mph) differ by factors 1.059 and 1.056, matching 5.17/4.89 = 1.057. Layout: 90-degree pushrod (OHV, 2 valves per cylinder) Gen V small-block V8, cross-plane crank, naturally aspirated, direct injection, Active Fuel Management. GM cylinder numbering: odd cylinders 1-3-5-7 on the left (driver's) bank = bank 0, even cylinders 2-4-6-8 on the right bank = bank 1 (Chevrolet Performance's Gen V LT1 harness views put the odd-side injector connector on the left bank and the even-side connector on the right). Combustion entries are listed in firing order 1-8-7-2-6-5-4-3 at even 90-degree intervals: banks L-R-L-R-R-L-R-L, bank 0 at 0/180/450/630, bank 1 at 90/270/360/540; GM's V4 (cylinder-deactivation) order 1-7-6-4 falls at 0/180/360/540, an even 180-degree subset, as it must. Conflict: the planning note expected a 6,600 rpm redline, but no GM document found states the LT2 redline; redline 6,500 rpm is from secondary press (CorvetteForum 2022: 'the base car's redline of 6,500 RPM', in an article quoting GM on the 4,000 rpm break-in limit). Estimated (not published in the sources used): limiter rpm 6,600 (GM's published 'Maximum Engine Speed 6600 RPM' for the closely related Gen V 6.2 LT1 crate engine, same bore, stroke, compression and firing order), limiter type fuel-soft with 150 rpm hysteresis, idle 700 rpm, and the DCT shift time 0.10 s (type default; GM only describes 'lightning-fast shifts').
